title: Azure SQL Authentication and Authorization
description: Understand SQL authentication, Azure Active Directory authentication, and how to manage database users and roles.

data.text: Azure SQL supports two authentication methods: **SQL authentication** (username and password stored in the database) and **Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) authentication** (identity-based access using Microsoft Entra ID). Azure AD is the recommended method because it eliminates passwords, supports conditional access, and integrates with managed identities.

SQL authentication uses a login and password created and stored in the master database. The server admin account is created when you provision the logical server. You can create additional SQL logins for specific databases or applications.

data.text: Azure AD authentication allows users and services to connect using their Azure AD identity. You create contained database users mapped to Azure AD identities. This supports Azure AD features like MFA, conditional access, and passwordless authentication.

terms.definition: A database user that is not tied to a server-level login, making the database more portable.
A server-level administrator assigned from Azure AD that manages AD-based access to all databases.
Built-in database roles that grant read-only or read-write access to all tables and views in a database.

data.title: Use Azure AD Everywhere
data.text: Create the server admin as an Azure AD user. Avoid SQL authentication in new applications. Use managed identities for services so no secrets are stored in connection strings.

data.title: Exercise: Compare Auth Methods
data.description: Create users with both SQL and Azure AD authentication and test access.
steps: Connect to your Azure SQL database as the server admin.
Create a SQL-authenticated user with SELECT permission on a table.
Assign an Azure AD admin at the server level in the Azure Portal.
Connect as the Azure AD user and confirm the same access works.
Remove the Azure AD user's permissions and confirm access is denied.
data.expectedOutcome: Two working authentication methods demonstrating the difference between SQL and Azure AD auth.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SQL auth stores credentials in the database; Azure AD auth uses Entra ID identities.
Azure AD supports MFA, conditional access, and passwordless flows.
Contained database users make databases more portable.
Use Azure AD admin at the server level to enable AD authentication.
data.takeaway: Azure AD authentication is the modern, secure way to access Azure SQL Database.
